source.title: Revisiting Residual Connections: Orthogonal Updates for Stable and Efficient Deep Networks
source.authors: Giyeong Oh; Woohyun Cho; Siyeol Kim; Suhwan Choi; Youngjae Yu

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains models from scratch and compares residual-update methods, reporting training-loss dynamics. It does not directly measure the claim versions’ training-classification-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The reported training-loss comparison bears on training progress, but it does not establish training classification error. Validation-accuracy tables and representational diagnostics do not measure the versions’ named outcomes. Initialization ablation reports validation accuracy, not learning speed or trainable depth.
record.test_reason: The study relies on residual connections to train its networks and evaluates a proposed residual-update modification. Its results do not test any version's specified comparison or outcome: faster training here follows a change in update geometry, not initialization, batch normalization, or adding identity shortcuts to plain networks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: orthogonal residual updates improve generalization and produce distinct training dynamics across the tested image-classification settings with modest computational overhead. These gains are not universal: some ResNetV2 comparisons show no improvement or lower validation accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Changes the residual update by projecting out the component parallel to the stream; compares this orthogonal update with standard linear residual updates.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture vary across experiments; initialization variants are compared for ResNetV2-50 on CIFAR-100. These reported outcomes are validation accuracy or internal diagnostics, not the claim versions’ named training-error outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2(a) reports that orthogonal residual updates achieve lower training loss in fewer iterations than standard residual updates for ViT-B trained from scratch on ImageNet-1k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal residual updates accelerate training-loss reduction relative to standard residual updates in the tested ViT-B ImageNet-1k setting.

record.problems: Training-loss comparison is figure-only and gives no numerical values or uncertainty in the text. The paper does not report training classification error, the main outcome named by the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Validation-accuracy comparisons in Tables 2–7, 10, and 12 and internal-dynamics plots in Figures 3–12 do not report a claim version’s named training-error, shortcut, width/local-minimum, learning-rate-stability, or batch-normalization-speed outcome; omitted.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels and dependencies on size, stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with plain-network depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization and normalization-free exceptions.
Initialization effects on plain-network learning speed and trainable depth. Appendix C.1 compares initialization recipes in residual networks using validation accuracy.

Recovery or divergence relative to initial stability thresholds, curvature reduction, and edge-of-stability dynamics. Table 3 reports validation accuracy across learning rates without these measurements.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched comparisons with Fixup. The final LayerNorm ablation measures a different intervention and outcomes.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply because none of V1–V6 is tested. Orthogonal residual updates are distinct from orthogonal weight initialization; internal norm stability does not establish the learning-rate stability behavior in V5.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error, including for corrupted or random labels, smaller models, or early stopping.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student study or comparison of student and teacher widths.
Does not compare plain networks against residual shortcuts for training error or test deep plain networks with special initialization or without normalization.
Initialization variants are compared on residual CNN validation accuracy; the paper does not test initialization effects on plain-network learning speed or trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability-threshold, curvature, or sharpness study.
No comparison of adding batch normalization to otherwise matched networks for training speed or learning-rate tolerance; the final LayerNorm comparison reports validation accuracy and norm dynamics.

rows.subject: ViT-B
rows.operation_detail: Compared standard linear residual updates with orthogonal residual updates; training-loss curves are shown.
rows.note: The text says the orthogonal update achieves significantly lower training loss in fewer iterations than the linear update. The plotted values are not stated numerically; training loss does not determine training classification error.
rows.check: This is a comparison of the study's proposed method with standard residual updates, outside V1–V6. Figure 2(a)'s caption explicitly reports lower training loss in fewer iterations for orthogonal updates, so the qualitative comparison is readable despite unavailable numerical values. It cannot establish near-zero training classification error or any other version's specified effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
